instructions: For each opaque pair, compare A and B. Identify every independently variable semantic distinction required to represent the difference. Do not assume any predefined ontology. For each distinction, test whether it can be reconstructed from the others without hidden metadata, unrestricted predicates, or implementation-specific conventions. Return your own smallest defensible semantic basis and actively try to falsify it.

pairs.A: An operation can execute and rule R allows it.
pairs.B: The same operation can execute but rule R rejects it.

pairs.A: A repair is allowed by rule R and the equipment is usable.
pairs.B: The same repair is allowed by rule R but the equipment is unusable.

pairs.A: A transaction is approved and required resources are available.
pairs.B: The same transaction is approved but required resources are unavailable.

pairs.A: A rule allowing an operation is applicable from 10:00 through 11:00.
pairs.B: The same rule is applicable from 12:00 through 13:00.

pairs.A: The same measurement is received from a calibrated instrument.
pairs.B: The same measurement is received from an unverified instrument.

pairs.A: A request times out and no reliable information establishes what happened externally.
pairs.B: A reliable later signal establishes that the requested operation did not succeed.

pairs.A: A remote action times out and its physical result is unresolved.
pairs.B: The remote action times out and later inspection confirms non-success.

pairs.A: Two systems have the same present condition but one reached it through recovery path X and the other through recovery path Y; the histories are retained.
pairs.B: Two systems have the same present condition and the same retained causal history.

pairs.A: Two machines have the same current condition but materially different retained maintenance histories.
pairs.B: Two machines have the same current condition and the same retained maintenance history.

pairs.A: An operation is allowed by rule R and all technical prerequisites hold.
pairs.B: The same operation is allowed by rule R but a required technical prerequisite does not hold.

pairs.A: Two operations are recorded with evidence of sequence A then B.
pairs.B: The same two operations are recorded without evidence sufficient to impose a total order.

pairs.A: A remote service is actually down and no signal about this fact has been received.
pairs.B: The same remote outage is actually present and a direct signal about it has been received.

pairs.A: An approval was sent and no reliable information establishes completion.
pairs.B: A reliable later record establishes that the approval was rejected.

pairs.A: At t1 and t2, two observations report the same condition and concern the same continuing service instance.
pairs.B: At t1 and t2, two observations report the same condition but concern two distinct service instances.

pairs.A: A request times out and the external result remains unresolved.
pairs.B: A request times out and a reliable later signal establishes non-success, making retry safe.

pairs.A: Two records with identical status concern the same contract.
pairs.B: Two records with identical status concern different contracts.

pairs.A: The same service instance is open at t1 and closed at t2.
pairs.B: The same service instance is open at t1 and remains open at t2.

pairs.A: The same machine is running at t1 and stopped at t2.
pairs.B: The same machine is running at t1 and remains running at t2.

pairs.A: A payment can be issued and rule R allows it.
pairs.B: The same payment can be issued but rule R rejects it.

pairs.A: Two inspections with the same reading concern the same machine.
pairs.B: Two inspections with the same reading concern different machines.

pairs.A: The same contract is active at t1 and suspended at t2.
pairs.B: The same contract is active at t1 and remains active at t2.

pairs.A: A control action causes physical movement.
pairs.B: The same control attempt produces no physical movement.

pairs.A: Two contracts have identical current status but materially different retained amendment histories.
pairs.B: Two contracts have identical current status and identical retained amendment histories.

pairs.A: Two occurrences are recorded and evidence establishes that the first precedes the second.
pairs.B: The same two occurrences are recorded but only a partial/concurrent ordering is justified.

pairs.A: The same statement comes from a verified record.
pairs.B: The same statement comes from an unverified report.

pairs.A: Two approvals are recorded and evidence establishes their sequence.
pairs.B: The same two approvals are recorded but concurrent processing remains possible.

pairs.A: A valve is actually closed and nobody has inspected it.
pairs.B: The same valve is actually closed and an inspection has been received.

pairs.A: A document is signed in the external world but no notice has been received.
pairs.B: The same signed document is accompanied by a received notice.

pairs.A: The same log statement is received from a source with verified provenance.
pairs.B: The same log statement is received from a source with materially different unverified provenance.

pairs.A: An approval applies during one specified time interval.
pairs.B: The same approval applies during another specified time interval.

pairs.A: A remote actuator command is issued and no reliable information establishes the physical result.
pairs.B: A later inspection reliably establishes that the actuator did not move.

pairs.A: A maintenance operation can be performed and rule R allows it.
pairs.B: The same maintenance operation can be performed but rule R rejects it.

pairs.A: An instruction is issued and the external transaction completes.
pairs.B: The same instruction is issued but the external transaction does not occur.

pairs.A: An authorization applies during one specified time interval.
pairs.B: The same authorization applies during a different specified time interval.

pairs.A: A submission times out and processing state remains unresolved.
pairs.B: A submission times out and a later reliable record confirms rejection.

pairs.A: A command is issued and the remote system changes state.
pairs.B: The same command is issued but the remote system does not change state.
